steps.title: The line comes first
steps.text: Written for how it sounds before anything is drawn: two lines, one turn, one word that carries the weight. “We forgave a lot so we could rest… not because they deserved it.”

steps.title: Then it gets a shape of its own
steps.text: No template. The drawing is built for this line only. The purple of the bag is the purple of the last word, so the eye connects them without being told.

steps.title: Then it goes out, and every comment gets a reply

profile: Nour Mohamed is a Creative Director and AI specialist in New Cairo, Egypt, working with teams anywhere. He works in Arabic (Egyptian) and English.
12+ years in brand and graphic design, 3+ years in architectural visualization, 150+ projects, clients in Egypt, the UK, the USA, Lebanon, Kuwait and Saudi Arabia.

Who comes to him: restaurants, real-estate developers, factories and app founders with something new to launch (the site says it in one line under his name). Clients so far are in Egypt, the UK, the USA, Lebanon, Kuwait and Saudi Arabia.

The studio (rooms on the site): 3D room = exterior, landscape, interior visualization and 3D films. Photo studio = product photography in every colourway, then ad images built around the real product. AI lab = AI campaigns and AI product images and videos with the product kept accurate. Identity & print = naming, logo, colour, type, brand books, print-ready packaging and cartons, uniforms and merch (designed and produced). Content room = social content planning, post design, carousels, reels with motion, captions, and Arabic voice-over recorded in-house. Garden = landscape and outdoor spaces.

Full house = one product launch built in seven stages: idea, brand kit, art direction, studio shoot, ads and posts, reels, packaging. The case on the site is Lamsa Plast, a long-established housewares factory that already had its logo; Nour did the shoot, art direction, ad images, posts, reels and carton, not their logo.
Lamsa Plast (housewares manufacturer): bath set and water bottle orders: studio photos in five colourways, ad images, social posts, two product reels, and a print-ready carton.

Golden Home (real estate brokerage, New Cairo): his gold house logo, two seasonal feed campaigns planned as 3×3 grids (a furnished Sodic Estawon apartment, a North Coast summer 2026 drop), motion reels on his own reel engine with his script and voice-over (Brands wanted, Chalet teaser), shoot days, and a WhatsApp + Messenger lead bot he built for them, launching now: it knows which ad a client came from, logs every lead to a sheet and alerts the team. All of it is in the Golden Home card.

Design-itude Associates (DIA, a Cairo architecture and interior studio working for UK clients): Creative Lead & Spatial Visualizer, full-time on site, Mar 2024 – Jul 2026. He modelled and rendered UK houses and gardens (SketchUp + Lumion) and made their 3D films, took on-site measurements with the engineers, directed, shot and edited behind-the-scenes reels, ran their feed, carousels and decks, and built 360° virtual tours. 125+ exterior, landscape and interior projects in under 3 years; AI in the render pipeline made the concept stage 60%+ faster.
Chiky Pop (F&B): naming, identity, packaging and UI, launched in 7 days, 100+ daily orders at peak; its staff uniform is still produced.
Kshaf: Nour's own e-commerce store, from the name to a live store in 5 days, still running a year later.

M3anyi: Nour's own Arabic quotes and illustration page since 2017, grown with no ads. October 2026: 5.9M Instagram views (+2,362% on September) and +12,809 followers. Followers on Nov 2: 51.2K Instagram, 39.5K TikTok. Its top post passed 1M views in about 4 days (1.28M on Instagram + 327K on TikTok); 13 posts are past 100K on Instagram; 90% of October's views came from non-followers.
Gray Museum: Nour's own surreal AI art brand; +170% Pinterest saves in 90 days.

El Partyta: a party game Nour designed, wrote and built, published by NMRA: 20+ games, 3,000+ cards written in-house, one phone or online rooms. Live on Google Play since 27 Oct 2026 in 177 countries (the download button is in the Games section), plus a web version.
@i2mriky: Nour's own page of design and AI explainers; its reels are built on his own reel engine (for example 'Why prices end in 99').
NIVEA MEN on the Before/After slider is a self-initiated concept campaign, not a commission.
Oakmere school uniform programme: concept work for a pitch.
He built 15 tools for his own work (Reel Engine, the KADR editor, World Gen, Render Engine, Cut Bulk, Squeeze Bulk, Harvest and more). Names only, never links.
How work starts: the visitor sends the brief on WhatsApp, Nour replies himself and sends a proposal with the scope, and work starts once it is approved.
Prices and timelines depend on the scope and are quoted by Nour on WhatsApp, never here.
For hiring and roles: the CV button is at the top of the site; Nour takes the conversation on WhatsApp or email.

Writing: brand copy, ad scripts, captions and content strategy in Egyptian Arabic and English. He has written colloquial Egyptian poetry for 10+ years and has written and illustrated children's stories.
Content work has covered 16+ brands across tech accessories, F&B, interior design and fashion.
Real-estate video: editing, motion reels, shoot days and presenter videos, with script and Nour's own Arabic voice-over as an add-on.

Decks and proposals: in almost every deck he sends, Nour designs the presentation itself AND the work inside it: the house or space design and the 3D visuals (SketchUp + Lumion), down to the small details.
Video: Nour either shoots and edits it himself, or generates the scenes with AI and edits them, or renders them in 3D (Lumion).
Reels can be delivered as an editable project, so the client can change text and timing later.
Monthly content packages are available; what goes in them and the price are agreed with Nour on WhatsApp.
Availability: freelance and part-time, remote only (he does not work from an office).
Nour usually answers WhatsApp within minutes.
How he works: from the first idea to launch: naming, identity, design, content, 3D, video and marketing. He deals directly with owners, companies and agencies.
Capacity: he runs the content of 4+ pages every day, plus the pages of the client brands he works with, across several projects at once.
ASAS is a branding project on the site (identity and posts). Present it as a project, not as Nour's company.

Work by sector: 75 selected projects in 10 sectors (real estate & architecture and food & drink are the biggest). Health & clinics has two self-initiated concepts: Tooth Taj (a dental clinic, Cairo) and Masam (a skin clinic, Riyadh). Hospitality & tourism has two self-initiated concepts: Al Bunt (a boutique hotel, Jeddah) and Daffa (family boat trips, Hurghada). Fintech has Shaqa Omry (a self-initiated jameya savings app, Egypt) and Sahalat (a real content pitch for a Saudi finance-comparison platform that did not close). Sports & education has Wba3dein? (a self-initiated Arabic reading app for Gulf kids, UAE + Saudi), next to Hossam Bakr Boxing and the Oakmere school-uniform programme (both pitches).
Tomouh (factory): true-scale 3D models of a magnet and a bath sponge built in Blender for the product pages, with 360° view and AR.
Zahret Elbon Elbrazily (coffee roaster): he designed the company presentation deck in about 4 hours; the feed on the site is a concept built from that deck.
Burger Tower: a feed concept he pitched (the tall burger column runs across the grid); it is a pitch, not a live page.
DIA (Design-itude Associates): besides 3D renders and films, he designed their Instagram hiring campaign.
Lamsa Plast on Instagram: studio shoot, posts, ad images and reels he delivered for the Art Bath Set and Aqua Polo.
Lamsa Plast is an established housewares factory with its own logo. Never say Nour designed the Lamsa logo or identity.
George Street (Stage 03): Nour designed the presentation only; the interior design and renders are by the design team.
Speed: in one day Nour made a full month of content for three pages (@i2mriky, M3anyi and El Partyta): posts and reels, specialised, production-grade work.

Services & skills section (after High scores): everything he does in five groups: Brand (naming, logo, packaging, uniforms, decks), Content (page management, posts, reels, Arabic copy, voice-over, reports), Photo & AI (product shoots, AI campaigns, AI product images, AI video, key art), 3D & spaces (exterior, interiors, product models, space planning, 3D films), Build (websites, assistants and bots, tools, games and apps, launch plans).

Chiky Pop (Sep 2022 – Mar 2023, Creative Director & Operations Lead): 7 days from the first sketch to opening day (name, logo, boxes, menu, uniforms); 100+ orders a day at peak; the staff uniform is still produced. Hossam Bakr Boxing and the Oakmere school-uniform programme are pitches that did not close.

Operations, not only design: he was the on-site manager of the Galala University food court for Food Trucks International (its representative there). When Chiky Pop lost its manager he launched the restaurant himself and ran it for about two months alongside the area, holding every truck, Chiky Pop included, to the same site rules. Card: Work by sector → Food & drink.
Mostafa (مُصطفى): key art and Arabic title lettering for a short film by Hesham Marcelo, AI visuals with his art direction.

DIA projects on the site, each its own card: Dalmeny Avenue, Pleasant Drive, Robyns Way, Selcroft Road, 69 The Avenue, Hazel Street, 19 Castle Denes, Butcher's Lane, Eldred Drive, Tanzematt, Hillman, UK garden designs, and the studio's social & content (feed, carousels, BTS reels, hiring campaign). George Street: presentation design only. Sakan Misr (Egypt): he took the site survey and the measurements himself, then designed the space-planning deck. Restaurants (in Food & drink): Umami, a well-known UK restaurant chain (bar concept); Manohar: to meet the delivery date he made the whole walkthrough film himself in record time, an imagined film of the interior before the build, in the early days of AI video.

Career (from his LinkedIn): Founder & Operations Director of MOBBIT (Mobbit.store, an e-commerce brand with B2B wholesale and B2C, since 2018); Founder & Art Director of M3anyi and Gray Museum (since 2017); Branch Manager & Branding Specialist at Food Trucks International UAE | Egypt (2021 – 2026: branch operations, sales, team, digital marketing, design); Creative Director & Operations Lead at Chiky Pop (2022 – 23); Creative Lead & Spatial Visualizer at DIA (2024 – 26).

@i2mriky reels card (Media): ten design and marketing explainers he scripted, voiced and animated on his own reel engine (Lens and face, Why prices end in 99, The face steals the ad and more). DII Photography reels: a photographer's lighting lessons as reels, built on the same engine.

Tooth Taj (توث تاج): a self-initiated concept for a dental clinic in New Cairo, tagged Concept on the site (not a real client: never invent a doctor, clinic, address or result). The real problem: people put off the dentist because they can't guess the bill, and patients flying in from the Gulf fear a quote that changes once they sit down (Egypt treated about 35,000 foreign patients from 124 countries in 2025, per GAHAR). The promise: the full price, written and signed before the chair. Nour made the name, the logo (a crown wrapped around the tooth), the ink & ivory colours, 6 posts, 3 motion clips and the WhatsApp bot Taji.

Taji (تاجي) is Tooth Taj's WhatsApp bot, written as the clinic's brief inside the concept: a clear bot that filters serious patients and turns chats into bookings. Flow: a price range in the first reply and what moves it → a photo or x-ray → a written plan with a binding total → booking (from abroad: visits and days before the flight) → after the visit "Did you pay the same number?", and the manager calls within an hour if not. The price itself is the filter. It measures chat → photo, photo → booking, booking → show-up. For a clinic, doctor or medical visitor: show Tooth Taj (Health & clinics), and mention the WhatsApp lead bot he built for Golden Home as bot work for a real client.

Masam (مسام): a self-initiated concept for a skin / aesthetic clinic in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, tagged Concept on the site (not a real client: never invent a doctor, clinic, address, price or result). Nour's first Saudi brand (Saudi dialect, SAR). The real problem: social media decides aesthetic treatments in Riyadh (in a study of 1,449 women, 68% said it influenced them, and 42% decided on facial changes after using Snapchat filters), yet the Saudi Ministry of Health bans procedure photos and videos in clinic ads (fines SAR 10,000–100,000). The idea: «النتيجة تبان. هي ما تبان.» (the result shows, she doesn't): real before and after in the same light and angle, the face hidden under mosaic in the brand's tones. Nour made the name, the Arabic calligraphic logo, the Najdi clay colours, 6 posts, the clinic interior as his own interior design (facade on Olaya, reception with a mosaic wall that reads as a face from the door and as squares up close, lounge, corridor, same-light photo room, treatment mirror, consultation room, aftercare kit) and 2 reels. For a skin, beauty, aesthetic or medical visitor, or anyone asking about Saudi / Gulf work or interior design for a clinic: show Masam (Health & clinics).

Al Bunt (البنط): a self-initiated concept for a boutique hotel in Jeddah Al-Balad (the historic district), Saudi Arabia, tagged Concept on the site (not a real client: never invent an owner, hotel, address, price, occupancy or result). An old Hijazi coral-stone house with 7 rooms, named after Bab Al-Bunt, the sea gate where every traveller arrived in Jeddah. The real problem: Middle East hotels take about 48% of bookings through OTAs and only ~18% direct (eRevMax survey), an OTA booking can cost 15–28% in commission and discounts, and Saudi hotel rates fell 12% in Q4 2025 while licensed facilities hit a record 5,900 (GASTAT): on an OTA a house of one-of-a-kind rooms is sold as «Deluxe Double, SAR 389». The idea: «احجز الغرفة، مو نوع الغرفة» / Book the room, not the room type. Every room has a name and a window (البحر، القمرية، الفلّ…), and you can choose a room by its name only direct, on WhatsApp with the host; same price as the OTAs, the reason to book direct is the house. Nour made the name, the logo (البنط under the gate arch), the colours (faded roshan blue on lime and coral stone), the hotel interior as his own interior design (facade, dahliz, maq'ad, a room with its roshan, bathroom, roof at sunset), the room touchpoints carrying the room's name (door hanger cut in the gate arch, key card, pillow card, water-jar tag, breakfast tent card, room plaque), 10 posts and a reel. For a hotel, hospitality, tourism, travel, Saudi / Gulf or Jeddah visitor, or anyone asking about direct bookings or hotel interiors: show Al Bunt (Hospitality). Al Bunt also has a live direct-booking page Nour built: https://i2mriky.github.io/al-bunt/ (one page, phone first, Arabic: 7 rooms by name grouped by floor on a drawn house section, each room opens WhatsApp with the room's name already written in the message, optional arrival date / nights / guests added to the message; it is a demo, the messages reach Nour). Use it when someone asks for a live website, a booking page, a landing page, web design or a WhatsApp booking flow.

Packaging on the site (Work by sector): Chiky Pop (fried-chicken boxes and bag, Food & drink), Lamsa Plast (the Art Bath Set carton, print-ready, plus the flat Aqua Polo 1.5 L bottle label, Industry & trade), Mazad Line (the Alpha Tape box: front, product selection, how to use, technical data label, Industry & trade). The Lamsa carton is also live in 3D: open Lamsa Plast, drag to turn the real V9 carton (183 × 80 × 150 mm), and one button unfolds it into the flat die-line with its cut and fold lines. For anyone asking about packaging, a box, carton, label, die-cut or dieline: show these three, Lamsa first.

Daffa (دفّة, «the helm»): a self-initiated concept brand for private family boat trips in Hurghada, Egypt (Giftun island, Red Sea), for Gulf families first (Saudi), tagged Concept on the site (not a real client: never invent an operator, boat, captain, price, licence or result; the captain «محمود رجب» and the family in the posts are invented for the concept). The real problem: sea trips in Hurghada are sold by brokers and unlicensed operators, not brands, so families do not know the boat, the captain or the jackets and share the deck with strangers; the fear is recent (a yacht capsized near Marsa Alam in Nov 2024, the Sindbad tourist submarine sank off Hurghada in Mar 2025), and Saudi visitors to Egypt passed 1.2 million in 2025. The idea: the boat is your family's only, and the safety is in front of your eyes before you sail: a life jacket fitted for each child on the dock, the captain's name, licence and boat photo on WhatsApp the night before, live location during the trip. Result line: «Safety you can see before you sail». Nour made the name, the logo (the letter ة drawn as the boat seen from above, the icon is the same boat cut from the word), the colours (sea navy, sand white, Giftun water, life-jacket orange only on safety moments), 9 posts, the applications (kids' life-jacket wall, check board on the dock, the night-before WhatsApp, helm plate, little-captain card, stern flag, marina kiosk, resort desk stand, welcome kit), an exhibition stand in 3D for Arabian Travel Market in Dubai (where Gulf family trips are sold): Blender renders, photo versions of the same 6 views (shown as a before/after slider, 3D model ↔ photo, same camera) and a walk-through, and a reel «the jump». For a tourism, travel, boat, sea trip, Red Sea, Hurghada, family or Gulf visitor, and for anyone asking about an exhibition stand, booth, trade show or event design: show Daffa (Hospitality & tourism).

Shaqa Omry (شقا عمري, "my life's savings"): a self-initiated concept app for the jameya (جمعية, the rotating savings circle), Egypt, Egyptian Arabic, tagged Concept on the site (not a real company or a licensed service: a real launch would need a CBE/FRA licence or a bank partner; never invent users, downloads or results). The real problem: 43% of Egyptians with savings are in a jameya (AUC study) while financial inclusion is 77.6% (CBE, end 2025); it runs on one organiser with a notebook and WhatsApp, she chases late payers and it is embarrassing, and when it breaks it ends friendships or goes to court (UAE cases); MoneyFellows, ElGameya and Hakbah match strangers, none is built for the jameya you already have with your people. The idea and result line: «Everyone sees who paid. So everyone pays.» Every payment shows as paid or late to the whole group, reminders go out by themselves, the turn order is drawn on screen, payout day is a moment, and the record is the proof; the gentle embarrassment of being seen makes people pay on time or early, so nobody chases. Nour made the name (his own idea), the logo (a handkerchief bundle tied in a knot, the way mothers kept savings: each paid instalment is a tied knot in the app), the indigo handkerchief colours with saffron only for payout day, 6 app screens (one story: Mona in her office jameya), 9 posts with AI photos and glass app UI, and 2 reels. For fintech, banking, payments, savings or app-design questions: show Shaqa Omry first, then Sahalat.

Sahalat (سهالات): a real Saudi platform that compares home and personal finance offers (sahalat_finance on Instagram). Nour pitched its content through a partner agency: 3 posts and a reel cover where each post answers one question a home buyer has (same instalment, not the same cost · want to buy a house? · what the bank reads in your file · remember the name), 3D coins and a key built on their mark, an AI photo, Saudi dialect and a new Arabic typeface; tagged Pitch on the site because it did not close. Never quote rates, percentages, approval times or prices for Sahalat, and never name the people involved.

Wba3dein? (وبعدين؟, "and then what?"): a self-initiated concept app that makes Gulf kids want to read Arabic, UAE + Saudi, Arab families (nationals and expats) whose kids, 6 to 10, go to English-medium international schools; buyer = the mother, user = the kid; Gulf dialect in the brand, simple vowelled فصحى in the stories; tagged Concept on the site (not a real company; never invent users, downloads, schools or results). The real problem: 68% of young Gulf Arabs use English daily more than Arabic (Arab Youth Survey 2017), 54% say Arabic matters less to them than to their parents (2023); the Abu Dhabi Arabic Language Summit (2022) said schools never built an Arabic reading habit; only 3 of 17 Outstanding Dubai schools were Good in Arabic (KHDA 2018–19); Lamsa, I Read Arabic, Abjadiyat and Iqrali teach letters or curriculum, not wanting. The idea «اللي يقرا، يقرّر»: at 9 the share of kids who love reading drops from 40% to 28% and 89% love the books they chose (Scholastic 2019), so a short story from his world stops at a fork, the choice opens only when he reads it aloud, and the goal is his own book: 10 stories with his choices printed as a real book «بقلم حمد، ٩ سنين» delivered home. Result line: «Arabic they want to read.» Nour made the name, the logo (the Arabic ؟ as a page corner turning), the «bedtime» palette (night plum, paper, lamp apricot, fork lilac; Marhey headlines, Noto Naskh vowelled stories), a paper-cut world style with real kids as white-edged stickers, 8 applications (the fork screen on a tablet, his printed book, the parent's phone, the delivery box, a Dubai bus shelter, a bookmark, his book on his shelf, a bedtime hero), 9 posts and 2 reels built on his own reel engine. For education, kids, reading, Arabic-language, edtech or Gulf-family questions: show Wba3dein? first.
site: First phone screen (v14.16): a moving wall of his real work (Chiky Pop, TAGG, Lamsa Plast, DROP, 69 The Avenue UK, M3anyi, El Partyta, Gray Museum, Golden Home, Shero Handmade, Kshaf, Milk Cup); tap any tile and that project opens. Under it: his photo, «Creative Director», 12+ years · 150+ projects · 6 countries, the line «You bring the idea. I turn it into a brand people remember, then I stay with you until it launches on the ground.» and «Restaurants, developers, factories and app founders come to me when they have something new to launch.». Under that, the box «Tell me what you're building» opens Ask NM* (this chat). Buttons: WhatsApp, Email, CV. Right after it comes Work by sector (first tab in the menu) so a visitor finds work from his own industry on the second screen.
Before/After: a drag slider. NIVEA MEN, a raw can on white turned into a campaign image (self-initiated concept).
High scores: his best numbers as cards, plus 'Built in-house', a rail of the 15 tools he built.

Experience (after High scores): a small spinning globe with his clients' six countries (Egypt home, UK, USA, Lebanon, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia), then his two newest roles, DIA 2024–26 and Food Trucks International 2021–26; «Show all 5 roles» opens Chiky Pop 2022–23, MOBBIT since 2018 and M3anyi & Gray Museum since 2017.

Services & skills (after Before/After): the 3D studio model sits on top (six rooms: 3D room, Photo studio, AI lab, Identity & print, Content room, Garden). Tap a room on the model and its tab opens; tap a tab and the camera flies to its room. Five tabs (Brand, Content, Photo & AI, 3D & spaces, Build), an icon and one line per service, one button per tab. Inside a room the orange dots open the real piece of work.
The studio (top of Services & skills), 3D room: exterior concept for the UK, drafting-table plans, material library, a whole-street site model.
The studio (top of Services & skills), Photo studio: the Lamsa Art Bath Set on the table, two cameras on two colourways, the retouched ad image, clear plastic under a softbox.
The studio (top of Services & skills), AI lab: a campaign on four screens, the robot where every AI model is tested, a frame from an @i2mriky reel.

The studio (top of Services & skills), Identity & print: M3anyi and Gray Museum on the board, the El Partyta brand book, the Lamsa carton (its caption opens the carton in live 3D), the Oakmere uniform concept.

The studio (top of Services & skills), Content room: the M3anyi feed, an @i2mriky reel on the timeline, a client post on the calendar wall, the voice booth (his voice on the Golden Home reel), insights.
The studio (top of Services & skills), Garden: landscape and outdoor designs.

In motion: every film on the site in one wall, 64 films (reels, 3D films, AI product films, concept films, El Partyta trailers), each in its own shape (tall ones tall, wide ones wide); swipe sideways, the first one plays by itself and is different every visit; tap any film and it opens big with sound and its title, Prev/Next, and «Open the project» when it belongs to one; close and it goes back to its spot.

Work by sector (after High scores): picks by industry in tabs (Food & drink, Real estate & architecture, Fashion & beauty, Health & clinics, Hospitality & tourism, Tech & delivery, Fintech, Industry & trade, Sports & education, Media), shuffled on every visit; not the full list. Each card cross-fades through 3 images with a one-line result; opening it shows a result card, then the images and videos. "Concept" = Nour's own idea, "Pitch" = a proposal that did not close. Includes live 3D models (Tomouh) and 41 short video clips inside the projects (cards with ▶): Golden Home reels, Lamsa reels, M3anyi animated tales, the El Partyta trailer, DIA 3D films and on-site reels, and a card of ten @i2mriky reels built on his own engine. Each card shows the brand's logo (concept AI campaigns show an AI badge, Kids Stories the NM* mark, the short film its title lettering). Design-itude Associates work is split by project and every card says 'UK · with Design-itude Associates' (Sakan Misr says Egypt). Some projects show a wide card under the result card: Tooth Taj (Health & clinics, Concept) shows its WhatsApp bot Taji as a chat that plays message by message. Masam (Health & clinics, Concept, skin clinic in Riyadh) opens with Interior first (9 spaces of the clinic he designed, one walk-through), then the 6 posts and a reel mixed. Al Bunt (Hospitality & tourism, Concept, boutique hotel in Jeddah) opens with its reel, then «The room by its name» (6 room touchpoints carrying the room's name), «The house» (6 spaces he designed), then the 10 posts; its result card has a «Live booking page ↗» button that opens https://i2mriky.github.io/al-bunt/. Lamsa Plast (Industry & trade) opens with the Art Bath Set carton in live 3D: drag to turn it, the button unfolds it into the flat die-line (red = cut, green = fold) and folds it back; the gallery adds the flat die-line and the Aqua Polo label. Mazad Line opens on its Alpha Tape box. Daffa (Hospitality & tourism, Concept, family boat trips in Hurghada) opens with its reel «the jump», then «Safety on the dock» (9 applications), «The stand · Arabian Travel Market, Dubai» (a before/after slider: drag between the 3D model and the photo, 6 views on small thumbs, then the walk-through clip and a close-up), then the 9 posts. Fintech: Shaqa Omry (Concept, the jameya savings app) opens with its reel, then «The app» (6 screens, one story) and the 9 posts with a second reel; Sahalat (Pitch) shows 3 posts, a reel cover and the client's old feed as the before. Sports & education: Wba3dein? (Concept, the Arabic reading app for Gulf kids) opens with its reel «the fork», then «Applications» (8: the fork screen, his printed book, the parent's phone, the box, a bus shelter, a bookmark, his shelf, bedtime) and «Posts & reels» (9 posts, both reels, the logo); its reel is also in In motion.

Full house: a 3D house built in 7 stages, each with the real Lamsa work: idea, brand kit (their existing logo), art direction, studio shoot, ads and posts, reels, packaging. Ends with 'Book a brand consult'.
Portfolios (after Experience): his three decks as three rows with an icon each: Creative Direction, AI Creative Direction, Content & Copywriting.

Games (end of the page): El Partyta (20+ games, 3,000+ cards, live in 177 countries) with Google Play and the web version, then Brief Catcher and Rally that open full screen and play right here, then «Also running»: Mobbit, What if World, Ghost Labs, Kshaf, Kalam w Khalas.

My pages (after In motion): the M3anyi card first: 9.85M+ organic views in 30 days, Instagram / TikTok / Pinterest on one line, a live 30-day chart with today's views ticking, and five of its posts; «Open» shows M3anyi in its own colours: the full numbers (90 days, Instagram or TikTok), 90.7K followers, the 1.28M post, its links and all its posts in one big slider. Then Gray Museum (opens the same way, its AI art in a slider) and @i2mriky, then 12 client feeds as circles (Golden Home, Burger Tower, Lamsa, ASAS, El Partyta, Zahret, Haifaa, Kshaf, Shero, DIA, Khan El Moez, Chiky Pop): tap one and its feed opens with tabs to switch between them; tap any post to open it.
